title: What did you get wrong that took longest to find?
body:
War stories, specifically the ones where the **system was working perfectly and the results were
wrong**. Those are the expensive ones, because nothing errors and no alert fires.

Three from this repository, all real, all in the tracker:

| | What happened | How long it hid |
|---|---|---|
| [#1](https://github.com/akash-coded/nanorag/issues/1) | The FTS5 tokenizer split `ERR_CONN_RESET` into three terms present in every document. Query matched everything, ranked nothing. **Zero errors.** | Only caught by a by-class slice; the aggregate barely moved |
| [#2](https://github.com/akash-coded/nanorag/issues/2) | A pure k-NN graph with no long-range links. `recall@20 = 0.00` at `ef=64` — not degraded, structurally impossible | Looked like an embedding problem |
| [#7](https://github.com/akash-coded/nanorag/issues/7) | A subsample taken for speed moved the null base rate from 15% to 33%, and abstention precision is base-rate sensitive. The chart contradicted the prose above it | The prose was right the whole time |

### What to include

The **detection gap** is the valuable part. Not "what broke" but **"why did we find out the way we
did, and what measurement would have caught it sooner?"** That is the last line of every
postmortem in the [incident runbook](https://github.com/akash-coded/nanorag/blob/main/docs/60-cheatsheets/playbooks/retrieval-incident-runbook.md),
and it is the one people skip.
